title: T-65B X-wing (Star Wars, A New Hope)
intro: The X-wing is a fictional starfighter from the Star Wars films: the Rebel Alliance's single-seat fighter with wings that split into an X, four laser cannons and proton torpedoes. The pilot sits under a long canopy with a two-handed yoke in front and switch-covered consoles left and right; an astromech droid (a small repair robot) rides in a socket behind. This guide follows the cockpit as seen in A New Hope (1977).

areas.name: Targeting computer scope
areas.text: The fold-down targeting scope in front of the pilot's eyes.

panels.name: Targeting computer scope
panels.text: A small screen on an arm that swings down in front of the pilot's eyes to help aim at a tiny target.
panels.context: In the film it is used for the attack run down the trench of the Death Star.

controls.name: Targeting scope
controls.text: This hood-shaped display swings down to the pilot's eyes. It shows a wire-frame picture of the trench and the target.
controls.context: It replaces looking out of the canopy for the last part of the attack.

controls.name: Range countdown
controls.text: Numbers on the scope count down the distance to the target, the small exhaust port.
controls.context: When the count reaches the right point the pilot fires the torpedoes.

controls.name: Targeting computer switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The scope swings down and shows the target picture.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The scope is stowed and the pilot looks out of the canopy.

controls.text: This switch turns the targeting computer on and swings the scope down in front of the pilot's eyes. Switching it off folds the scope away.
controls.context: In the film Luke switches it on for the trench run and later switches it off again to aim by himself.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: Small screens and readouts under the canopy rim.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: A few small screens and lights in front of the pilot: the sensors, the droid's messages and the state of the ship.
panels.context: The pilot glances at them between looks out of the canopy.

controls.name: Sensor scope
controls.text: This round screen shows where targets and chasing enemy fighters are around the X-wing.
controls.context: It warns the pilot of fighters coming from behind, outside the view.

controls.name: Astromech message screen
controls.text: This screen shows the droid's beeps translated into words, so the pilot can read what the droid says.
controls.context: The droid behind the pilot reports problems and repairs through it.

controls.name: Status lights and readouts
controls.text: Small lights show the state of systems, shields and damage.
controls.context: The film does not explain each light; together they tell the pilot whether the fighter is healthy.

areas.name: Side consoles
areas.text: Rows of switches and lights on both sides of the seat.

panels.name: Side consoles
panels.text: Banks of switches and lights beside the seat, plus the switch that opens the wings.
panels.context: The pilots flip them during the start-up and in the fight; the film shows them busy but does not explain every switch.

controls.name: S-foil control

positions.name: ATTACK
positions.text: The wings are open in the X shape; the fighter is ready to fight.

positions.name: CRUISE
positions.text: The wings are closed flat for normal travel.

controls.text: This control opens the X-wing's wings (S-foils) into the X shape for attack, or closes them flat for cruising.
controls.context: In the film the leader orders the pilots to lock the S-foils in attack position before the battle; open wings spread the four cannons apart.

controls.name: Left console switches
controls.text: A bank of toggle switches on the left side of the seat. The pilot flips them during start-up and in combat.
controls.context: The film does not show what each switch does; they belong to the fighter's systems.

controls.name: Right console switches
controls.text: A second bank of toggles and lights on the right side of the seat.
controls.context: Like the left bank, it is part of the busy cockpit the film shows without naming each switch.

areas.name: Astromech droid socket
areas.text: The droid socket behind the canopy.

panels.name: Astromech droid socket
panels.text: A round socket behind the canopy where a small droid rides along.
panels.context: The droid helps the pilot with navigation and repairs during the flight.

controls.name: Astromech droid (R2 unit)
controls.text: An R2 unit, a small robot, sits in the socket. It carries navigation data and repairs the fighter in flight.
controls.context: In the film R2-D2 fixes a damaged part of Luke's fighter during the battle.

areas.name: Control yoke and throttle
areas.text: The hand controls the pilot flies with.

panels.name: Control yoke
panels.text: The two-handed yoke the pilot steers with.
panels.context: Both hands stay on it; the fire buttons are under the thumbs.

controls.name: Control yoke
controls.text: Pushing the yoke forward or pulling it back tips the nose down or up; turning it rolls and banks the fighter.
controls.context: The yoke sits on a column in front of the pilot, held with both hands.

controls.name: Fire buttons
controls.text: Buttons on the yoke grips under the thumbs fire the four laser cannons.
controls.context: With the wings open the four cannons fire from the wingtips.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: This stands for the control that sets the craft's speed.
panels.context: A New Hope does not show this control clearly; the catalog adds it so a joystick set has a place for the speed.

controls.name: Throttle (not clearly shown)
controls.text: This axis stands for the craft's speed: forward for faster, back for slower. The screen does not show where the real control sits, so its place is a guess.
controls.context: On a stick and throttle set this is the throttle lever; in the work itself the pilot is mostly seen with both hands on the flight controls.
